title: Private deploy networking incident notes - VPC peering / DNS / TLS / egress
content:
Summary:
Observed customer private deployment unable to reach hosted control plane endpoints intermittently. Symptoms: model start failures, "failed to fetch model manifest", TLS handshake errors from runtime logs, and DNS NXDOMAIN for some control-plane hostnames from customer VPC. Impact: 1 customer (staging) deploys failing, potential production risk if routes collapse.

Timeline / quick notes:
- 2026-03-03 09:12 UTC: Alert: repeated container restarts on private node pool.
- 2026-03-03 09:18 UTC: Customer reports model downloads failing with TLS errors.
- 2026-03-03 09:25 UTC: Eng oncall (Maya) started triage, asked for nslookup/traceroute outputs.
- 2026-03-03 09:40 UTC: Confirmed intermittent NXDOMAIN and TCP timeouts to control-plane endpoints.

Commands tried (raw):
- dig +short control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example
  -> (intermittent) "" or 10.2.3.45
- dig @10.0.0.2 control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example
  -> NXDOMAIN (when failing)
- nslookup control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example 10.0.0.2
  Server: 10.0.0.2
  Address: 10.0.0.2#53

  ** server can't find control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example: NXDOMAIN

- curl -v https://control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example/health
  * About to connect() to control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example port 443 (#0)
  *   Trying 10.2.3.45...
  * TCP_NODELAY set
  * connect() timed out!
  * Failed to connect to control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example port 443: Connection timed out

- openssl s_client -connect control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example:443 -servername control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example
  (when IP reachable) -> OK, cert CN=control-plane.redwood-hosted.example, verify return:1
  (when failing) -> connect:errno=110 

- traceroute -n 10.2.3.45
  1  10.0.0.1  0.4 ms  0.4 ms  0.3 ms
  2  10.1.100.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.2 ms
  3  * * *  (packet loss / blackhole)

- aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcde12345
  -> peering-0fghij alive, status: active

- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcde12345
  -> route to peer (10.2.0.0/16) present on rt-0a1b2c3d (expected)

- sudo iptables -L -n -v
  -> OUTPUT chain policy ACCEPT, no obvious block rules.

- tcpdump -i eth0 port 53 or port 443 -w /tmp/capture.pcap (ran for 2m during outage)
  -> saw repeated DNS queries to 10.0.0.2 with no UDP reply; subsequent TCP fallback to 53 (dns over tcp) also no reply. When DNS resolved to IP, TCP SYNs to 10.2.3.45 saw SYN then no SYN-ACK (~RST from upstream sometimes).

Observed error snippets (from runtime logs):
- "error fetching model manifest: tls: handshake failure"
- "dns: lookup control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example: no such host"
- "http: server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client" (rare)
- "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" (single instance when customer used custom CA for internal resolver)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Intermittent DNS resolution failures from customer resolver (10.0.0.2) — either overloaded or conditional forwarding misconfigured for host suffixes. Evidence: NXDOMAIN from customer's resolver; tcpdump shows no UDP response.
2) VPC peering route asymmetry / blackhole for some AZs — traceroute shows hop drop at hop 3; route tables show route present but maybe missing on specific ENIs or AZ route table associations.
3) Egress (NAT / firewall) throttling or connections tracked and dropped — SYNs reaching remote but no SYN-ACK; could be reverse path or ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT.
4) TLS mismatch due to SNI rewriting or internal proxy returning plain HTTP -> "http: server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client" indicates proxy might be intercepting some TLS. Occurred rarely; more likely secondary symptom.

Work done / what to check next (immediate):
- Ask customer infra to check the DNS server health (10.0.0.2): logs, CPU, socket drops, whether floods or rate limits are in effect.
- Confirm route table associations across all subnets in affected AZs (aws ec2 describe-route-tables + describe-subnets).
- Get tcpdump from customer on both inside VPC and at peered VPC edge to see whether DNS/443 packets are leaving their VPC.
- Check customer NAT gateways / transit gateway rules for port exhaustion: monitor NAT bytes/connections via CloudWatch.
- If DNS is flaky, add temporary /etc/hosts entry on affected nodes to pin control-plane host -> IP to validate whether DNS is root cause (quick test). Documented hack: echo "10.2.3.45 control-plane-api.redwood-hosted.example" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts && systemctl restart runtime.service

Longer-term follow-up:
- Recommend customer set up conditional forwarding for redwood-hosted.example to Redwood resolver (if using on-prem DNS) or ensure AmazonProvidedDNS is used for recursive resolution.
- Add instrumentation: if resolver returns NXDOMAIN/timeout 3x in 1m, runtime should switch to fallback DNS (internal cache or Redwood resolver via peered interface).
- Add more robust connection tracing on our control-plane to correlate incoming SYNs to the TLS handshake logs (to see whether packets arrive and get dropped after handshake start).

Notes / pointers to related artifacts:
- INC-4821: customer ticket with screenshots and logs (link above).
- JIRA-1234: follow-up task to add DNS fallback behavior to private runtime.
- Slack thread: customer-reported issue with some packet captures attached.

Triage status: ongoing. Primary lead: Lucas (me) + Maya. Maya has asked customer to provide packet captures from both sides and to check health of 10.0.0.2. Samir to verify route table associations and AZ-specific ENI/route propagation.

Immediate reproduction steps (dev env):
1) In staging VPC that mirrors customer's CIDRs, create resolver VM and deliberately drop replies from resolver using iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp --dport 53 -j DROP to simulate DNS blackhole.
2) Run runtime on private node and attempt model download; observe DNS NXDOMAIN/timeouts and TLS failures.
3) Validate /etc/hosts workaround; confirm model download succeeds when DNS resolved.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some connections see HTTP response to HTTPS client? Is there an intercepting proxy in path doing TLS offload? Need customer network team to confirm any transparent proxies.
- Is there rate limiting per-source IP at Redwood control-plane edge that could manifest as intermittent resets? Need to check edge rate-limit logs.
- Are we seeing any MTU / fragmentation issues causing TLS handshake to fail late? (lower MTU test pending)

Next steps (owners):
- Customer: provide tcpdump from resolver (10.0.0.2) and peered VPC edge. (Requested, pending)
- Samir: double-check route table associations across subnets in affected AZs and post results to JIRA-1234.
- Maya: collect runtime logs with timestamps and map to packet capture times.
- Lucas: add /etc/hosts quick test to dev-staging to prove DNS root cause.

If anything changes I will update this doc. Repeatable steps and raw outputs are saved to /tmp/networking-triage-2026-03-04/ on my laptop and uploaded to the incident ticket.

-- Lucas
